newsitem.title: USA: Turner challenges Murdoch to boxing match.
newsitem.headline: Turner challenges Murdoch to boxing match.

text.p: Media mogul Ted Turner challenged on Friday his long-time rival Rupert Murdoch to a boxing match in order to settle their differences once and for all.
In light-hearted remarks to a group of Hollywood entertainment leaders, Turner volunteered to donate the proceeds to charity.

"What do you think about Rupert Murdoch and Ted Turner putting on gloves and getting into the ring," the Time Warner Inc vice chairman, who also owns the Atlanta Braves National League baseball league franchise, asked the crowd.
"Nobody's seen two 60-year olds fight in a long time," Turner said. "It would be good entertainment and we could give all the money to charity. To the indigenous actors' home."
Turner began his remarks by promising not to say anything about Murdoch, a habit that has repeatedly got him into trouble in the past.
But then he went right on to ask if anyone in the audience would like to see Murdoch own the Dodgers.
Turner has often brought the bitter professional rivalry with Murdoch down to a personal level, and last year caused an outrage by likening him to Adolf Hitler.
He later apologized for the remarks -- not to Murdoch but to Jewish groups.
Murdoch, the News Corp. chairman known for his tabloid newspapers and racy television programming, is negotiating with Peter O'Malley to buy the the Los Angeles Dodgers for $350 million.

If he succeeds, it would bring his rivalry with Turner to a new level, making them direct competitors in the National Baseball League, and complicating their longstanding fight over television viewers.
When Turner began airing Braves games on nationwide cable television, he won increased exposure to the Turner Broadcasting System and made them what he calls "America's Team."

During a court battle last year over cable rights in New York, Turner referred to Murdoch in depositions as a "slimy character" and "very dangerous person" who "shamelessly" used the power of the media to advance his wealth and influence.
